- Any new blocking work added to a hot path (the pre-push git hook runs on every `git push`).
- In the new tests: repeated subprocess spawns (`git ls-remote` / `git log` per ref inside a loop) where one invocation would do.

Efficiency-only review of the diff. Four findings, ranked. The headline: **the pre-push hot path costs exactly the same as before**; everything I found is on the migrate path or in tests.

---

**1. (Medium) Queue resolve + ref partition now run twice on the migrate path — the caller with the largest N**
`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/worktree-calm-harbor-6f61/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:454-458` (new gate) feeding `manual_commit_opf_refs.go:36-84` and then `manual_commit_push.go:476-492`.

With OPF enabled, one flush now does the queue work twice and the ref lookups three times, over the identical ref set:

| work | `RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF` | `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checkpoint.PushQueueForRepo` | yes (`opf_refs.go:36`) | yes (`push.go:477`) — cheap, `resolveGitCommonDir` is memoized |
| queue file lock + read + parse | `Peek()` (`opf_refs.go:41`) | `Drain()` (`push.go:481`) |
| `partitionLocalRefs` → N × `repo.Reference` | `opf_refs.go:84` | `push.go:492` |
| a further N × `repo.Reference(name, true)` | `opf_refs.go:86-92` | — |

Concrete cost per flush of N queued refs: **2 flock+read cycles instead of 1, and 3N `repo.Reference` calls where N would do.** On a reftable repo that is not a file read — `gitrepo.reftableStorer.Reference` (`gitrepo/reftable.go:259-292`) spawns up to two git subprocesses per lookup with no cache, so **6N subprocesses instead of 2N**. For a migration backfill of 200 refs that is ~800 wasted spawns.

Magnitude honesty: the duplication is **pre-existing** on the pre-push path — `runOPFForCheckpointRefs` already did all of it — so the diff introduces no new work per push there. What the diff does is land the same pattern on `doctor migrate`'s "push now" (`doctor_migrate.go:100`), which is precisely the largest-N caller, since it fires right after migrating every historical checkpoint (`len(result.Migrated)`).

Cheaper alternative: `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` already computes `existing` inside the rewrite. Resolve the queue and partition **once** in the two callers and pass `(queue, existing, stale)` into both the rewrite and `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` (which would take them instead of calling `PushQueueForRepo`/`Drain`/`partitionLocalRefs` itself). That drops one flock+read and 2N ref lookups per flush. Second-best, cheap and local: have `partitionLocalRefs` return the resolved `*plumbing.Reference` values it already fetched, killing the redundant lookup at `opf_refs.go:86`.

**2. (Low — do not fix) `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs` now loads settings twice**
`manual_commit_push.go:440` (`resolvePushSettings` → `settings.Load`) and `:455` → `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` → `opfPrePushDecision` → `settings.Load` (`:227`).

Delta is **+1 `settings.Load` per invocation, and only when `redact.OPFEnabled()`**. `settings.Load` is genuinely uncached, but the expensive parts underneath it are all memoized by the time the second call runs: `paths.WorktreeRoot` (`paths/paths.go:87-92`), `gitdir.CommonDir` (`gitdir/gitdir.go:69-75`), and the tracked-file probe (`settings/opf_command_trust.go:206-222`). So the second load is ~3 small `readConfined` reads plus a JSON parse and merge — **no subprocess** — on a once-per-command, TTY-gated path (`doctor_migrate.go:80-100`) that is about to spawn a network `git push`. Tens of microseconds against seconds.

For the pre-push path the delta is **zero**: `runOPFForCheckpointRefs` already called `opfPrePushDecision`, so pre-push still does exactly 2 loads (one in `prePush`'s `resolvePushSettings`, one in the gate).

The cheaper alternative exists but is not worth it: thread the loaded settings through by adding `opfCfg *settings.OPFSettings` to `pushSettings` (which `resolvePushSettings` currently loads and discards) and giving `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` a settings parameter. That widens a struct and a shared signature to save three file reads on a path that runs once per migration. Leave it.

**3. (Informational) No new blocking work on the pre-push hook**
`manual_commit_push.go:406-410`. The rewrite of `runOPFForCheckpointRefs` → `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` is strictly a bool→error signature change; the same `opfPrePushDecision` and the same `RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF` run in the same order, and `warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld` simply moved from callee to caller. When OPF is off, both call sites are still short-circuited by the cheap global read `redact.OPFEnabled()`. Nothing to flag — recording it because it was the specific risk asked about.

**4. (Low — negligible) Two subprocesses per ref in the new test loop**
`refs_push_test.go:350-354`. Each iteration spawns `git ls-remote` (`remoteRefHash`, `:315`) plus `git log -1 --format=%B` (`remoteCommitMessage`, new at `:391`) — 4 subprocesses for the fixture's 2 refs, growing 2× per ref.

Cheaper alternative: one `git -C <bare> for-each-ref --format='%(refname)%0a%(contents)' refs/entire/` returns every ref name *and* its full commit message in a single spawn, so the whole loop becomes one substring assertion per ref against one captured output. (Alternatively, mirror the sibling test at `:380-386`, which correctly hoists a single bare `git ls-remote` out of its loop, then batch the messages with one `git log --no-walk --format=%B <h1> <h2>`.)

Magnitude: the test already spawns roughly a dozen git processes in `setupRepoWithCheckpointRefs` plus the real push, so this saves ~2 spawns out of ~15 — call it noise. Worth doing only if `remoteCommitMessage` is touched again; not worth a round trip on its own.

---

Nothing else in the diff adds work: both new gates are behind `redact.OPFEnabled()`, so an OPF-disabled repo pays nothing on either path, and both `Peek` and the rewrite return immediately on an empty queue.
